arxiv-2208-12704.title: On semibiproducts of magmas and semigroups
arxiv-2208-12704.creator: N. Martins-Ferreira
arxiv-2208-12704.description: Abstract . A generalization to the categorical notion of biproduct, called semibiproduct, which in the case of groups covers classical semidirect products, has recently been analysed in the category of monoids with surprising results in the classification of weakly Schreier extensions. The purpose of this paper is to extend the study of semibiproducts to the category of semigroups.

arxiv-2508-03947.title: Control Closure Certificates
arxiv-2508-03947.creator: Vishnu Murali (✉), Mohammed Adib Oumer, and Majid Zamani
arxiv-2508-03947.description: Abstract This paper introduces the notion of control closure certificates ( C 3 \text{C}^{3} ) to synthesize controllers for discrete-time control systems against ω \omega -regular specifications. Typical functional approaches to synthesize controllers against ω \omega -regular specifications rely on combining inductive invariants (for example, via barrier certificates) with proofs of well-foundedness (for example, via ranking functions).

arxiv-2602-12852.title: WebClipper: Efficient Evolution of Web Agents with Graph-based Trajectory Pruning
arxiv-2602-12852.creator: Junjie Wang, Zequn Xie, Dan Yang, Jie Feng, Yue Shen, Duolin Sun
arxiv-2602-12852.description: Abstract Deep Research systems based on web agents have shown strong potential in solving complex information-seeking tasks, yet their search efficiency remains underexplored. We observe that many state-of-the-art open-source web agents rely on long tool-call trajectories with cyclic reasoning loops and exploration of unproductive branches.

pmc-11396294.title: Prevalence and factors influencing long COVID among primary healthcare workers after epidemic control policy adjustment in Jiangsu, China
pmc-11396294.creator: Hualing Chen, Yongkang Qian, Beier Lu, Rongji Ma, Pengcheng Miao, Mingwang Fu, Haijian Guo, Ya Shen, Zhengkai Shen, Yan Li, Biyun Xu, Yongjie Zhang, Jinshui Xu, Bingwei Chen
pmc-11396294.description: ObjectiveThe persistent symptoms arising from COVID-19 infection pose a substantial threat to patients’ health, carrying significant implications. Amidst the evolving COVID-19 control strategies in China, healthcare workers (HCWs) endure considerable stress. This study aims to evaluate the prevalence of long COVID infections and their influencing factors among primary HCWs after epidemic control policy adjustment in Jiangsu.

pmc-12526379.title: Triterpene and Caffeoylquinic Acid Constituents Contribute to the Cognitive-Enhancing, but Not Anxiolytic, Effects of a Water Extract of Centella asiatica in Aged Mice
pmc-12526379.creator: Wyatt Hack, Lucas Kuhnau, Jesus Martinez, Luke C Marney, Jaewoo Choi, Arshia R Sohal, Seiji Koike, Thuan Nguyen, Claudia S Maier, Amala Soumyanath, Nora E Gray, Carla Masala
pmc-12526379.description: Background/objectives: A water extract of the plant Centella asiatica (CAW) has been shown to improve cognitive deficits in aged mice when administered for 5 weeks in drinking water. However, the contribution of the constituent compounds within CAW to the beneficial effects of the extract remains unelucidated.

pmc-12664417.title: An integrated development framework for data-driven model predictive control of thermal zones in buildings
pmc-12664417.creator: Peter Klanatsky, François Veynandt, Christian Heschl
pmc-12664417.description: The increasing integration of renewable energy systems into the power grid necessitates enhanced demand-side flexibility in buildings. Data-driven model predictive control (DMPC) has emerged as a promising approach for such energy management task. To advance research in this field, this paper introduces a comprehensive simulation environment designed to facilitate the development and evaluation of DMPC solutions for buildings.

pmc-13463459.title: Machine learning-based prediction of intraoperative blood transfusion in major surgery: exploiting clinical variables and systemic inflammatory indices
pmc-13463459.creator: Laura Verzellesi, Lucia Merolle, Marco Bertolini, Valeria Trojani, Davide Schiroli, Andrea Nitrosi, Erminia Di Bartolomeo, Margherita Genitoni, Mauro Iori, Roberto Baricchi, Chiara Marraccini
pmc-13463459.description: BackgroundIntraoperative blood transfusion is common in major surgery. Predicting transfusion risk may improve perioperative management, optimize blood use, and enhance surgical planning. Machine Learning (ML) offers promising tools for individualized risk prediction.AimTo develop and validate an ML model predicting intraoperative transfusion risk in major surgery using clinical variables and inflammatory indices.

pmc-13511156.creator: Johanna G. Rodríguez, Thomas Renné
pmc-13511156.description: Polyphosphate (polyP) is an evolutionarily conserved linear polymer of orthophosphate residues with diverse functions across organisms from bacteria to mammals. In addition to its roles in phosphate and energy storage, polyP has been implicated in thrombosis, inflammation, cancer, metabolism, cytoskeletal regulation, and neurodegenerative diseases.
